title: Krishnamurti and Osho: Two Teachers of Freedom
description: What J. Krishnamurti and Osho taught about freedom, awareness, thought, love and meditation, where their teachings meet, and where they sharply part.
audience: Curious beginners. No background in philosophy or spirituality needed.

chapters.title: Highlights
chapters.summary: Nine cards on two teachers of freedom: what binds us, how each says to see through it, and where they meet and part.

chapters.title: Two Teachers, One Map
chapters.summary: Tour the core ideas of both teachers and how they connect, then rebuild the map from memory.

chapters.title: The Pathless Land Case
chapters.summary: Why did the young man raised to be a 'World Teacher' walk away in 1929? Crack the case and find what Krishnamurti taught instead.

chapters.title: Zorba the Buddha
chapters.summary: Everyday situations seen through Osho's teaching: meditation, desire, love, religion and celebration.

chapters.title: Krishnamurti or Osho?
chapters.summary: Ten situations, two teachers: work out how each would respond, and why they differ.

chapters.title: Islands of Awareness
chapters.summary: One island per big idea from both teachers, hands-on activities, then a final exam.

objectives: Explain what each teacher meant by freedom, conditioning, thought and awareness
Tell apart Krishnamurti's choiceless awareness from Osho's catharsis-then-witnessing
Describe the 1929 dissolution of the Order of the Star and what Krishnamurti taught instead
Predict how each teacher would respond to an everyday situation, and say where they agree and part

glossary.definition: The habits of thought and feeling a mind picks up from family, culture, religion and experience, which both teachers say stand between us and seeing clearly.
Krishnamurti's term for watching what is happening, inside and out, without judging, choosing or trying to change it.
The sense of becoming something later; Krishnamurti held that it is the root of fear and conflict.
Osho's hour-long technique that moves from chaotic breathing and catharsis to stillness and celebration.
Osho's word for observing thoughts and emotions without becoming them; close to, but reached differently from, choiceless awareness.
Osho's image of a complete human being: worldly joy and inner silence in one person.
The organisation built around Krishnamurti as the coming World Teacher, which he dissolved in 1929.
